newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Gulf/Midco diffs firm on fire hype.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Gulf/Midco diffs firm on fire hype.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast and Midcontinent cash products differentials heated up late Wednesday on a pipeline scheduling deadline and continued hype over a fire earlier this week at a Kansas refinery.
The small fire at National Cooperative Refinery Association's 74,000-bpd plant hobbled gasoline production, adding strength to gasoline and distillate differentials in the two hubs.
NYMEX gasoline settled 1.10 cents a gallon higher at 61.12 cents. August heating oil ended 0.58 cent up at 53.28 cents.
U.S. GULF
Gasoline prices grew volatile in Houston late Wednesday, with the highly liquid "M1" regular conventional southern-grade erasing all the deterioration in differentials marked earlier in the day.
Some traders said the flurry of buying interest after the NYMEX close came from short covering ahead of Wednesday's scheduling deadline for placement of M1 on Colonial Pipeline's back 21st cycle.
Prompt barrels of M1 were heard done late in the day at 2.85 cents under August NYMEX gasoline or about the level at which differentials stood at the start of trade.
That compared with deals heard as weak as 4.25 cents under in the early afternoon.

On the distillate front, differentials were steady to perhaps a touch firmer amid talk that price strength connected to the partial outage at NCRA's refinery was spreading to the Gulf from the Midcontinent.
Prompt 74-grade in Houston remained around Tuesday's level of 1.35.
MIDCONTINENT
Midcontinent unleaded gasoline and distillate differentials firmed in light afternoon trade, pressured by the NCRA fire and by a buyer-heavy market.

The fire led to concerns of distillate availability in the near future. In Group Three, low sulphur popped by more than a penny, with deals heard done at 2.00 cents over August NYMEX futures. Sellers were at 2.50 cents over the screen.
"Rumor has it the fire at NCRA may also affect distillates," said a cash broker. It is unclear how long NCRA will be at curtailed capacity.
In Chicago, low sulphur diesel differentials were up about a half cent to put buyers at 0.25 cent below the print.
Group Three prompt unleaded differentials also firmed on the fire hype, rising 0.50 cent in the day to 0.50/0.75 cent over August NYMEX futures. Deals were heard done as high 1.00 cent.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Prompt regular conventional M2 gasolines eased modestly by late Wednesday, although prompt reformulated A2 gasoline differentials ended stronger, traders said.

The regular conventional gasoline inched higher earlier in the day, possibly reaching as high at 3.50 cents under the August NYMEX, though offers fell back to at least 4.00 cents under by the end of the day.
"I think that was just in sympathy with the early weakness in the M-grades in the Gulf today," one Harbor player said.
However, prompt A2 reformulated gasoline found active buying interest, peaking at 2.35 cents over late in the day.
Market players pointed to continued tightness in the MTBE market, despite the modest pullback in the gasoline additive's price late in the day.
--New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1620
